label: First copy step after <DEL> (input = orig token 0, outputting token 1), longer sequences
explanation: Fires exclusively at step t = L+1, the first copy step after the delimiter, where the fed-back input is the first original token and the model must output original token 1 (recall_idx == 1 gives recall 1.0, precision 0.65). It never fires in the original phase, on the <DEL> step, or at any later copy step. Within that step, activation and firing rate grow with sequence length: nearly every L=8-9 sequence fires, L=3-5 rarely fire and weakly; restricting to L >= 6 gives F1 0.87 and 96% mass recall on dev. Input-token identity (e.g. 0, f) mildly raises magnitude; top activations are all L=9 sequences. Missed activations are short (L=4-5) sequences with low activation; false positives are L=6-7 sequences where it stays just below threshold.

issues: The claims check out. The unit fires only at recall_idx == 1, at most once per sequence. On test, recall_idx==1 alone gives recall 1.0 and precision 0.644. (recall_idx==1)&(L>=6) gives P 0.858, R 0.884, F1 0.871, mass recall 0.965, matching the report. The top 12 activations are all L=9.

Firing rate at recall_idx==1 by L on test: L=5 0.30, L=6 0.57, L=7 0.87, L>=8 0.995. So most false positives come from L=6 sequences (about 7k of the 9.4k), with L=7 next. This is a graded effect with no sharp cutoff at L=6.

The 'small' first-token effect is understated near the threshold. At L=6, first token in {0,f,b,o} fires 95% of the time versus 57% overall, and every top activation starts with 0 or f. The token mainly controls intensity, so how far it pushes a step over the threshold depends on L. It does not change the explanation's structure.
None of the misses or false positives form a class beyond the L and first-token gradient. Misses are low-magnitude L=4-5 steps holding 3.5% of the mass.
